rules.noDoubleCounting: When a text belongs to multiple groups, a profile must use its declared precedence rule or maximum applicable multiplier; group multipliers are never added or multiplied together.
rules.authorityBoundary: Group membership records reception and transmission. It is not itself evidence of truth, falsity, inspiration, suppression or fraud.

groups.label: Protestant 66-book canon
groups.members: The 39-book Hebrew Bible ordering used in Protestant Old Testaments plus the 27-book New Testament.
groups.notes: Used only as one reception boundary; not treated as the universal definition of scripture.

groups.label: Broadly shared Jewish-Christian and New Testament core
groups.members: Books shared across the Protestant, Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Ethiopian biblical traditions, while acknowledging differences of ordering, language and textual form.
groups.notes: A reception-overlap group, not a claim that every community assigns identical status or text form.

groups.label: Catholic deuterocanonical books
groups.notes: Some members and additions are also received in Eastern and Ethiopian traditions.

groups.label: Eastern Orthodox broader Old Testament reception
groups.notes: Exact lists and liturgical status vary by church and edition.

groups.label: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo broader canon
groups.notes: The narrow/broader canon distinction and English naming of books require edition-level care; Ethiopian Meqabyan is not the same work as Greek Maccabees.

groups.label: Second Temple and early Jewish pseudepigrapha
groups.notes: The label describes modern corpus organization, not one ancient canon or uniform theology.

groups.label: Nag Hammadi codices
groups.notes: Nag Hammadi is a manuscript collection, not a single Gnostic canon. Texts differ in date, school, genre and theology.

groups.label: Related late-antique revelatory and esoteric Christian texts
groups.notes: Kept separate from the Nag Hammadi manuscript corpus even where themes overlap.
